title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: vignette demonstrates complete workflow systematically evaluating identifying optimal testing strategies quarantined individuals. methods shown based analysis scripts inst/examples/ illustrate : Generate possible testing schedules within constraints Evaluate schedule parallel computational efficiency Identify optimal schedules different scenarios quarantine durations Visualize compare results approach allows policy-makers balance test resources transmission reduction.

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
code: library(isolatr) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(ggplot2) library(foreach) library(doParallel)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: First, define epidemiological intervention parameters:
code: # Epidemiological parameters n.ind <- 100000  # Large sample for stable estimates TP <- 1.2        # Transmission potential k <- 0.2         # Dispersion parameter (superspreading)  # Vaccination parameters (NSW example) p.vac.idx <- 0.723   # Index case vaccination probability p.vac.sc <- 0.723    # Secondary case vaccination probability vacc.cor <- 0.9      # Household vaccination correlation  # Vaccine effectiveness VE.trans <- 0.4      # Against transmission VE.inf <- 0.72       # Against infection  # State the.state <- "NSW"  # TTIQ scenarios to evaluate the.scenarios <- c("optimal", "partial", "current_nsw_case_init")  # Quarantine durations to evaluate quarantine.durations <- c(14, 7)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: Use test.designs() systematically generate valid testing schedules:
code: # Maximum possible test days max_days <- max(quarantine.durations)  # Minimum spacing between tests (e.g., 2 days) min.space <- 2  # Generate all schedules with 1, 2, or 3 tests all.times3 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 3,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  all.times2 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 2,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  all.times1 <- test.designs(   times = 1:max_days,   n = 1,   min.space = min.space,   t1.prior.to = max_days )  # Combine all schedules all.times <- all.times3 %>%   filter(Var1 <= 5) %>%   add_row(     all.times2 %>%       mutate(Var3 = Inf) %>%       filter(Var1 <= 5)   ) %>%   add_row(     all.times1 %>%       mutate(Var2 = Inf, Var3 = Inf)   )  nn <- nrow(all.times) print(paste("Evaluating", nn, "testing schedules"))

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: Now loop quarantine durations TTIQ scenarios, evaluating testing schedules parallel:
code:
results_list <- list()  for (hq.d in quarantine.durations) {   for (ts in the.scenarios) {      cat(paste("
Evaluating", ts, "scenario with", hq.d, "day quarantine
"))      # For 7-day quarantine, filter out schedules that extend beyond day 7     if (hq.d == 7 && ncol(all.times) == 3) {       all.times_filtered <- all.times %>%         select(-Var3) %>%         distinct() %>%         filter(Var1 <= hq.d & (Var2 <= hq.d | is.infinite(Var2)))       nn <- nrow(all.times_filtered)     } else {       all.times_filtered <- all.times     }      # Step 1: Run base simulation (once per scenario/duration combination)     set.seed(1)  # For reproducibility     CQ.output <- CQ.sim2(       n.ind = n.ind,       TP = TP,       k = k,       p.vac.idx = p.vac.idx,       p.vac.sc = p.vac.sc,       vacc.cor = vacc.cor,       VE.trans = VE.trans,       VE.inf = VE.inf,       quarantine.duration = hq.d,       the.scenario = ts,       the.state = the.state     )      # Step 2: Evaluate all testing schedules in parallel     cl <- makeCluster(4)  # Use 4 cores (adjust based on your machine)     registerDoParallel(cl)      tic <- Sys.time()      output <- foreach(       i = 1:nn,       .combine = rbind,       .packages = c("tidyverse", "isolatr")     ) %dopar% {       CQ.sim.test.times(         CQ.sim.output = CQ.output,         n.ind = n.ind,         test.times = all.times_filtered[i, ] %>% as.numeric(),         VE.trans = VE.trans,         the.scenario = ts       )     }      toc <- Sys.time() - tic     cat(paste("Completed in", round(toc, 2), attr(toc, "units"), "
"))      stopCluster(cl)      # Combine schedules with results     results <- cbind(all.times_filtered, output) %>%       mutate(         scenario = ts,         q.duration = hq.d       )      results_list[[paste(ts, hq.d, sep = "_")]] <- results   } }  # Combine all results all_results <- bind_rows(results_list)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
code: # Clean up column names colnames_base <- c("t1", "t2", "t3") if (ncol(all.times) <= 3) {   colnames(all_results)[1:3] <- colnames_base[1:3] }  # Add number of tests all_results <- all_results %>%   mutate(     t2 = case_when(       is.na(t2) ~ Inf,       TRUE ~ t2     ),     t3 = case_when(       is.na(t3) ~ Inf,       TRUE ~ t3     )   ) %>%   mutate(n.tests = 3 - is.infinite(t2) - is.infinite(t3))  # Identify optimal schedules optimal_schedules <- all_results %>%   group_by(scenario, q.duration, n.tests) %>%   filter(IPq == min(IPq)) %>%   mutate(TT = paste0("(", t1, ",", t2, ",", t3, ")")) %>%   mutate(TT = gsub(pattern = ",Inf", replacement = "", x = TT)) %>%   select(scenario, q.duration, n.tests, TT, IPq, sdIPq, mean.cases)  print(optimal_schedules)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
code: optimal_schedules %>%   mutate(     scenario = factor(       scenario,       levels = c("optimal", "current_nsw_case_init", "partial"),       labels = c("Optimal delays", "NSW case-initiated delays", "Partial delays"),       ordered = TRUE     )   ) %>%   mutate(     q.duration = factor(       q.duration,       levels = c("14", "7"),       labels = c("14-days", "7-days"),       ordered = TRUE     )   ) %>%   ggplot() +   aes(x = TT, y = IPq, fill = as.factor(n.tests)) +   geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single")) +   scale_x_discrete("Test Strategy") +   scale_y_continuous("IPq (Infection Potential in Quarantine)") +   scale_fill_discrete("Number of Tests") +   facet_grid(q.duration ~ scenario, scales = "free_x") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(     text = element_text(size = 12),     axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)   )

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: number tests, visualize test timing affects IPq:
code: # Identify optimal schedules for highlighting the.opt <- all_results %>%   mutate(id = row_number()) %>%   mutate(     q.duration = factor(       q.duration,       levels = c("7", "14"),       labels = c("7-day", "14-day"),       ordered = TRUE     )   ) %>%   group_by(q.duration, scenario, n.tests) %>%   filter(IPq == min(IPq)) %>%   pivot_longer(cols = t1:t3) %>%   filter(is.finite(value))  # Plot for 3-test schedules plot.the.scenario <- "optimal"  all_results %>%   filter(scenario == plot.the.scenario, n.tests == 3) %>%   mutate(id = row_number()) %>%   mutate(     q.duration = factor(       q.duration,       levels = c("7", "14"),       labels = c("7-day", "14-day"),       ordered = TRUE     )   ) %>%   pivot_longer(cols = t1:t3) %>%   ggplot() +   aes(x = value, y = IPq, group = id) +   geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +   geom_point(aes(colour = name), alpha = 0.6) +   geom_point(     data = the.opt %>% filter(scenario == plot.the.scenario, n.tests == 3),     aes(x = value, y = IPq, group = id),     size = 3,     colour = "black"   ) +   geom_line(     data = the.opt %>% filter(scenario == plot.the.scenario, n.tests == 3),     aes(x = value, y = IPq, group = id),     size = 1,     colour = "black"   ) +   scale_y_continuous("IPq") +   scale_x_continuous("Test day for PCC", breaks = seq(1, 14, by = 1)) +   facet_grid(q.duration ~ .) +   scale_colour_manual(     "Test Number",     values = c("darkviolet", "green4", "darkorange"),     labels = c("1", "2", "3")   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "top")

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: Identify schedules perform within 2% optimal: shows range test timings achieve near-optimal performance, providing flexibility implementation.
code: near_optimal <- all_results %>%   group_by(scenario, q.duration, n.tests) %>%   arrange(IPq) %>%   mutate(efficiency = IPq / min(IPq)) %>%   filter(efficiency <= 1.02) %>%   mutate(     T1 = paste0(min(t1), "-", max(t1)),     T2 = paste0(min(t2), "-", max(t2)),     T3 = paste0(min(t3), "-", max(t3))   ) %>%   mutate(     T2 = gsub("Inf-Inf", "-", T2),     T3 = gsub("Inf-Inf", "-", T3)   ) %>%   select(scenario, q.duration, n.tests, T1, T2, T3, efficiency) %>%   distinct() %>%   arrange(desc(q.duration), desc(n.tests))  print(near_optimal)

title: Finding Optimal Testing Strategies
text: systematic evaluation, can derive several insights: Optimal test timing varies scenario: Faster TTIQ systems allow later first tests Test spacing matters: Tests strategically spaced capture infections different stages Diminishing returns: Adding 3rd test provides smaller marginal benefit adding 2nd Robustness: Multiple schedules often perform nearly well single optimum

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: vignette provides -depth explanation mathematical statistical models underlying isolatr package. Understanding details help : Interpret results correctly Choose appropriate parameter values Assess model limitations Extend modify model needs

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: simulation models following process: Index case infection: individual (primary close contact) exposed COVID-19 Incubation period: Time exposure symptom onset Contact tracing: Index case identified quarantined Household transmission: Potential spread within household quarantine Testing schedule: Active testing may detect infection early Passive detection: Symptom development leads healthcare seeking Onwards transmission: Undetected infections may cause tertiary cases key question: many tertiary infections occur undetected secondary cases?

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: number secondary cases index case ii follows negative binomial distribution: ncases,∼NegBin(k,TP)n_{cases,} \sim \text{NegBin}(k, TP) : - TPTP = transmission potential (mean) - kk = dispersion parameter (smaller = overdispersion/superspreading)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time infection index case infection secondary case jj: GIij∼LogNormal(μ=1.376,σ=0.567)GI_{ij} \sim \text{LogNormal}(\mu=1.376, \sigma=0.567) gives median GI ≈ 3.96 days, calibrated Australian COVID-19 data.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time infection symptom onset index case ii: IPi∼LogNormal(μ=1.63,σ=0.5)IP_i \sim \text{LogNormal}(\mu=1.63, \sigma=0.5) Median IP ≈ 5.1 days.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Household size index case ii state ss: HHi,s∼Fs(h)HH_{,s} \sim F_s(h) Fs(h)F_s(h) empirical CDF household sizes state ss, derived Australian census data.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Index case vaccination status: Vi∼Bernoulli(pvac,idx)V_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_{vac,idx}) Secondary case vaccination (household members): Vij∼{CorrelatedBinary(Vi,ρ)household memberBernoulli(pvac,sc)otherwiseV_{ij} \sim \begin{cases} \text{CorrelatedBinary}(V_i, \rho) & \text{household member} \\ \text{Bernoulli}(p_{vac,sc}) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} ρ\rho household vaccination correlation.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Probability infection given exposure: P(infection∣exposure)=(1−VEtrans⋅Vi)⋅(1−VEinf⋅Vj)P(\text{infection} \mid \text{exposure}) = (1 - VE_{trans} \cdot V_i) \cdot (1 - VE_{inf} \cdot V_j) : - VEtransVE_{trans} = vaccine effectiveness transmission (reduces infectiousness) - VEinfVE_{inf} = vaccine effectiveness infection (reduces susceptibility)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Secondary infections classified based timing relative isolation: Pre-isolation (tinf<tisot_{inf} < t_{iso}): Occur index case quarantined Household (tiso≤tinf<tiso+Qdurationt_{iso} \leq t_{inf} < t_{iso} + Q_{duration}): Occur quarantine household members Post-quarantine (tinf≥tiso+Qdurationt_{inf} \geq t_{iso} + Q_{duration}): Occur quarantine ends proportion pre-isolation post-quarantine infections randomly reassigned household (probability 0.5), household size limit. accounts uncertainty exact infection timing.

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Test sensitivity varies viral load, changes infection course. model sensitivity using logistic function: Let CC = time peak viral load (days symptom onset): C=min(IP,3.5)⋅U(0,1)C = \min(IP, 3.5) \cdot U(0,1) U(0,1)U(0,1) uniform random variable. Time since infection test tt: st=tiso+t−1−IP−Cs_t = t_{iso} + t - 1 - IP - C tt test day (relative isolation start). Test sensitivity: P(positive∣infected,t)={11+exp(−(1.5+2.2st))st<0 (pre-peak)11+exp(−(1.5−0.22st))st≥0 (post-peak)P(\text{positive} \mid \text{infected}, t) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-(1.5 + 2.2s_t))} & \text{} s_t < 0 \text{ (pre-peak)} \\ \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-(1.5 - 0.22s_t))} & \text{} s_t \geq 0 \text{ (post-peak)} \end{cases} Pre-peak: sensitivity increases viral load rises Post-peak: sensitivity decreases viral load declines

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: testing schedule 𝐭=(t1,t2,…,tn)\mathbf{t} = (t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n): Calculate sensitivity pip_i test time tit_i Simulate test results: Ri∼Bernoulli(pi)R_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_i) First positive test: tfirst=min{ti:Ri=1}t_{first} = \min\{t_i : R_i = 1\} (∞\infty negative) Add turnaround time: tfirst+TTATt_{first} + T_{TAT} Add delays: tfirst+TTAT+Tothert_{first} + T_{TAT} + T_{} : - TTATT_{TAT} = test turnaround time (scenario-specific) - TotherT_{} = interview + notification delays (scenario-specific)

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time detection symptoms (without active testing): Tpassive,ij=tinf,ij+DpassiveT_{passive,ij} = t_{inf,ij} + D_{passive} DpassiveD_{passive} sampled scenario-specific empirical distribution representing: - Time infection symptom onset - Time symptoms healthcare seeking - Time healthcare seeking confirmation

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: Time index case infection isolation: Tiso,=DactiveT_{iso,} = D_{active} DactiveD_{active} sampled scenario-specific distribution representing: - Time index case detection - Time interview index case - Time identify notify close contacts - Time quarantine close contacts

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: undetected secondary infection jj index case ii, infection potential : IPij=FGI(min(tdetect,ij,tpassive,ij)−tinf,ij)⋅TP⋅(1−VEtrans⋅Vj)IP_{ij} = F_{GI}(\min(t_{detect,ij}, t_{passive,ij}) - t_{inf,ij}) \cdot TP \cdot (1 - VE_{trans} \cdot V_j) : - FGIF_{GI} = CDF generation interval distribution - tdetect,ijt_{detect,ij} = time detection (via testing symptoms) - tinf,ijt_{inf,ij} = time infection - CDF term represents proportion onwards transmission occur detection Total Infection Potential Quarantine (IPq): IPq=1nind∑=1nind∑j∈undetectedIPijIPq = \frac{1}{n_{ind}} \sum_{=1}^{n_{ind}} \sum_{j \\text{undetected}} IP_{ij}

title: Model Details and Methodology
text: TTIQ scenario empirical distributions : Time isolation (active detection) Time passive detection Test turnaround time Interview delay Notification delay distributions derived : - optimal: Best-case assumptions (rapid tracing, fast testing) - partial: Moderate delays - current_nsw_case_init: NSW empirical data distributions stored : - Sampled values (turnaround times) - Cumulative probabilities (inverse transform sampling)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: isolatr package provides tools simulating COVID-19 transmission quarantine evaluating different testing strategies. quick start guide walk basic workflow.

title: Quick Start Guide
text: typical workflow consists three steps: Simulate transmission dynamics using CQ.sim2() Evaluate testing strategies using CQ.sim.test.times() CQ.sim.notest() Compare results across different strategies

title: Quick Start Guide
text: First, simulate transmission 1000 index cases (primary close contacts) quarantine: output data frame one row per secondary infection:
code: set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility  sim_results <- CQ.sim2(   n.ind = 1000,                  # Number of index cases to simulate   TP = 3.0,                      # Transmission potential (mean secondary cases)   k = 0.25,                      # Dispersion (lower = more superspreading)   p.vac.idx = 0.7,               # Probability index case is vaccinated   p.vac.sc = 0.7,                # Probability secondary cases are vaccinated   vacc.cor = 0.8,                # Household vaccination correlation   VE.trans = 0.5,                # Vaccine effectiveness against transmission   VE.inf = 0.7,                  # Vaccine effectiveness against infection   quarantine.duration = 14,      # Quarantine period (days)   the.scenario = "optimal",      # TTIQ scenario   the.state = "NSW"              # Australian state ) head(sim_results)  # Check infection types table(sim_results$who)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: Now can evaluate effective specific testing schedule : output shows: - IPq: Infection Potential Quarantine (lower better) - sdIPq: Standard deviation - mean.cases: Mean undetected cases per index case
code: # Test on days 1, 3, and 6 strategy_1 <- CQ.sim.test.times(   CQ.sim.output = sim_results,   n.ind = 1000,   test.times = c(1, 3, 6),   VE.trans = 0.5,   the.scenario = "optimal" )  print(strategy_1)

title: Quick Start Guide
text: Let’s compare several testing strategies:
code: # Define strategies strategies <- list(   "Days 1,3,6" = c(1, 3, 6),   "Days 2,7" = c(2, 7),   "Days 1,5,10" = c(1, 5, 10),   "Day 6 only" = 6 )  # Evaluate each results <- lapply(names(strategies), function(name) {   out <- CQ.sim.test.times(     CQ.sim.output = sim_results,     n.ind = 1000,     test.times = strategies[[name]],     VE.trans = 0.5,     the.scenario = "optimal"   )   out$strategy <- name   out$n_tests <- length(strategies[[name]])   return(out) })  # Add no-testing baseline baseline <- CQ.sim.notest(sim_results, n.ind = 1000,                           VE.trans = 0.5, the.scenario = "optimal") baseline$strategy <- "No testing" baseline$n_tests <- 0  # Combine and display comparison <- bind_rows(results, baseline) print(comparison %>% arrange(IPq))

title: Quick Start Guide
text: TP (Transmission Potential): Mean number secondary cases per index case. Typical values: 1-5 k (Dispersion): Controls overdispersion. Lower values (0.1-0.3) indicate superspreading VE.trans: Vaccine effectiveness transmission (0-1) VE.inf: Vaccine effectiveness infection (0-1)

code: # Define testing strategies to compare strategies <- list(   "Day 1, 3, 6" = c(1, 3, 6),   "Day 2, 7" = c(2, 7),   "Day 1, 5, 10" = c(1, 5, 10),   "No testing" = NULL  # Baseline )  # Evaluate each strategy results <- lapply(names(strategies), function(name) {   if (name == "No testing") {     out <- CQ.sim.notest(sim_results, n.ind = 1000, VE.trans = 0.5, the.scenario = "optimal")   } else {     out <- CQ.sim.test.times(sim_results, n.ind = 1000, test.times = strategies[[name]],                              VE.trans = 0.5, the.scenario = "optimal")   }   out$strategy <- name   return(out) })  comparison <- bind_rows(results) print(comparison %>% arrange(IPq))

text: function models impact testing schedule transmission quarantine. index case, : Determines time first positive test using internal testing function Adds test turnaround time delays (interview, notification) Filters secondary infections occur detection Calculates infection potential undetected case infection potential (IPq) represents expected number tertiary infections undetected secondary cases, accounting : Generation interval distribution Time remaining detection Transmission potential (TP) Vaccine effectiveness transmission Lower IPq values indicate effective testing strategies.

title: Evaluate Quarantine Testing Strategy — CQ.sim.test.times
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # First, run the simulation set.seed(42) sim_results <- CQ.sim2(   n.ind = 1000, TP = 3.0, k = 0.25,   p.vac.idx = 0.7, p.vac.sc = 0.7, vacc.cor = 0.8,   VE.trans = 0.5, VE.inf = 0.7,   quarantine.duration = 14,   the.scenario = "optimal" )  # Evaluate a testing strategy: test on days 1, 3, and 6 evaluation <- CQ.sim.test.times(   CQ.sim.output = sim_results,   n.ind = 1000,   test.times = c(1, 3, 6),   VE.trans = 0.5,   the.scenario = "optimal" )  print(evaluation) } # }

what: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: Simulates COVID-19 transmission index cases secondary cases quarantine, accounting household structure, vaccination status, isolation timing, testing/tracing scenarios.

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
code: CQ.sim2(   n.ind,   TP,   k,   p.vac.idx,   p.vac.sc,   vacc.cor,   VE.trans,   VE.inf,   quarantine.duration,   the.scenario,   the.state = "NSW" )

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: n.ind Integer. Number index cases (primary close contacts) simulate. TP Numeric. Transmission potential - mean number secondary cases per index case (analogous R0 fully susceptible population). k Numeric. Dispersion parameter negative binomial distribution secondary cases. Lower values indicate greater overdispersion (superspreading). p.vac.idx Numeric. Probability index case vaccinated (0-1). p.vac.sc Numeric. Probability secondary case vaccinated (0-1), non-household contacts. vacc.cor Numeric. Correlation coefficient (0-1) vaccination status within households. Higher values mean household members likely vaccination status. VE.trans Numeric. Vaccine effectiveness transmission (0-1). Reduces probability vaccinated index case transmits infection. VE.inf Numeric. Vaccine effectiveness infection (0-1). Reduces probability vaccinated secondary case becomes infected. quarantine.duration Numeric. Duration quarantine period days. .scenario Character. TTIQ scenario name. Must one : "optimal", "partial", "current_nsw_case_init". .state Character. Australian state territory household size distribution. Default "NSW". See abbreviate_states valid values.

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: data frame one row per secondary infection (among unprotected individuals), containing following columns: Index case ID (1 n.ind) vacc.status Vaccination status index case (0 1) inc.period Incubation period index case (days) iso.time Time isolation index case (days) ncases Number secondary cases index case hh.size Household size index case inf.times Time infection secondary case (days since index case infection) Classification infection: "preiso" (isolation), "hh" (household member), "postiso" (quarantine) sc.vac.status Vaccination status secondary case (0 1) det Time passive detection secondary case

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: function implements stochastic simulation model COVID-19 transmission quarantine. model: Samples individual-level characteristics (vaccination, incubation period, isolation time, household size) index case Samples number secondary cases negative binomial distribution Samples generation intervals (time successive infections) lognormal distribution calibrated Australian COVID-19 data Classifies infections occurring isolation, within household quarantine, post-quarantine Models household-correlated vaccination status Calculates passive detection times based TTIQ scenario Filters infections based vaccine effectiveness function uses following epidemiological distributions: Incubation period: Lognormal(μ=1.63, σ=0.5) Generation interval: Lognormal(μ=1.376, σ=0.567) - Australian COVID-19 baseline Number secondary cases: Negative Binomial(size=k, μ=TP)

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
text: Important: function previously included hard-coded set.seed(1) removed. Users set seed calling function reproducibility required.

title: Community Quarantine Simulation for Primary Close Contacts — CQ.sim2
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Simulate 1000 index cases with moderate transmission set.seed(42) results <- CQ.sim2(   n.ind = 1000,   TP = 3.0,   k = 0.25,   p.vac.idx = 0.7,   p.vac.sc = 0.7,   vacc.cor = 0.8,   VE.trans = 0.5,   VE.inf = 0.7,   quarantine.duration = 14,   the.scenario = "optimal",   the.state = "NSW" )  # Examine distribution of infection times summary(results$who) } # }
